subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
Since this is a static model, I can skip joints entirely and just use parts with position and direction attributes. I'm planning the truck's proportions, facing forward with a length around 8 meters, width about 2.6 meters, and sketching out the height next.

Now I'm working out the geometry details: six wheels across three axles, chassis boxes, and a cab built using an extruded side profile with a sloped hood, windshield, and roof outline, plus a cargo bed with armor plates, a turret, sensors, glowing neon strips, and missile pods, all positioned relative to a local z-origin along the truck's length.

Working out the windshield tilt angle so it leans back correctly, then placing the glass box with a slight outward offset. I'll add dark blue glowing boxes for the side windows positioned on each side of the cab.

Now I'm building the wheels with rotated cylinders for tires and rims, adding lug bolts, a cyan glow ring, and tread blocks via a loop, positioning each wheel slightly outside the frame's half-width.

Working out rotation to align tread blocks radially, then laying out the chassis frame dimensions relative to wheel radius and tire width, adding mudguards above the wheels, and sketching the cab and armored cargo container placement along the z-axis.

I'm planning to add a roof turret, missile pods, and rear ramp to the cargo box, using the clockwork kit's metal and panelled materials for a gunmetal body with magenta and cyan neon accents, plus a glow kit for lit elements. For the cab, I'm listing out details like vented hood slats, a glowing grille, cyan headlight boxes with a light bar, a spiked bull bar, roof light bar, antenna, twin exhaust stacks, and doors.

I'm continuing the cab details with mirrors and decal textures, then moving to the cargo section with ribbed panels, a top rail, roof hatches, a lathe-built RCWS turret, dual six-tube missile pods, angled side armor, neon strips, red rear glow lights, a rear ramp, under-side fuel tank cylinders, drive shafts, and axles. I'm also planning five textures total—an emblem, hazard stripes, a license plate reading "77-2077", HUD windshield glow lines, and a vent grille—and setting up textured planes on each side of the vehicle with directional flags so decals face outward correctly.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders, then working through ground-clearance math to make sure the wheel geometry's bottom vertex sits exactly at y=0 given a 12-sided cylinder and a 0.62 radius/center. I'm also laying out the chassis z-extents—nose, cab, gap for exhaust and fuel tank, and cargo bed—before starting on the cab's extrusion origin.

Writing truck part generation code, including panelled metal paint for the hull, a glowing roof light bar made of small boxes, and neon strip boxes running along the sides at x=±1.22.

Adding armor plates above the wheels, then designing the roof turret with a cylindrical base and ring, a boxy body, and twin barrel cylinders with muzzle details.

Now I'm placing cab roof details: a light bar, antenna, and exhaust stacks positioned in the gap between cab and cargo. Then I'm working out the front nose face geometry and grille placement on the slanted front.

I'm adding headlights, bumper, hazard decal, and bull bar spikes to the front, then checking whether the front wheel's position and size cause it to clip into the cab body given their respective x-ranges.

Since there's slight overlap, I'll add fender boxes over the wheels to mask it, then move to the underbody: frame rails, axles, differential spheres, and fuel tanks sized and positioned to clear the wheels. After laying out the geometry I'll move to texture SVGs for the emblem, number plate, hazard stripes, and windshield HUD overlay.

Writing door decal and finalizing code with loops...
